participations ne donnant pas le contrôle

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
IFRS readers know IFRS 10: one control model, and a choice between full and partial goodwill. U.S. GAAP uses two control models and allows only full goodwill. Many exam traps come from these two differences.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT   Minority interest, حقوق الأقلية, intérêts minoritaires
These older terms still appear in many MENA and French texts. The exam uses noncontrolling interest (الحصص غير المسيطرة, participations ne donnant pas le contrôle). It is equity, never a liability.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: Orontes's cold-chain entity
Step 1. Suppose a logistics entrepreneur owns all the shares of Orontes Cold-Chain Logistics SPV. The shares cost $100,000.
Step 2. Banks lend $9,900,000, guaranteed by Orontes. Equity is only 1% of the funding, and Orontes decides routes and customers: the SPV is a VIE.
Step 3. Orontes has the power and bears the losses through its guarantee, so it is the primary beneficiary.
Check. Orontes consolidates the SPV although it owns no shares. The entrepreneur's $100,000 is NCI. Figure F16-03 sets out the analysis.
Is equity at risk enough to finance the activities?
No: third-party equity is 100,000, only 1% of total funding
Do the equity holders direct the key activities?
No: Orontes decides routes and customers
Orontes has both power and exposure to significant losses

EXAM TRAP   Control traps
Test the VIE model before counting votes.
The primary beneficiary needs power AND significant economics, not one of them.
Under U.S. GAAP, less than half of the votes is not control, even if the other owners are widely spread.

EXAM TRAP   'Equity consolidation' is the equity method
The LOS phrase 'equity consolidation' means the equity method: one line, no NCI. It is not full consolidation. Also, joint ventures use the equity method, not proportionate consolidation.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: the acquisition-date elimination
Step 1. Remove Levant's equity of $7,300,000: it is not owned by outsiders to the group, except through NCI.
Step 2. Add the equipment step-up of $1,200,000 and goodwill of $1,400,000.
Step 3. Remove Orontes's investment of $8,000,000 and record NCI of $1,900,000 in equity.

EXAM TRAP   Elimination traps
Eliminate intercompany items in full, not only the parent's share.
Downstream profit reduces only the parent's share; upstream profit is shared with NCI.
For an equity-method investee, remove only the investor's share of the profit.

WATCH: NOT YET TESTABLE   Consolidation: not yet testable
ASU 2025-03 changes how to identify the acquirer when the acquired company is a VIE; it is not testable before about January 2028. In January 2026 the FASB began research on bringing the VIE and voting models closer together. That is a proposal only. ASU 2023-05, on joint venture formations, affects only the joint venture's own statements.
